evidence_identity.reference_snapshot_scope: The snapshot identifier was supplied by the assignment; this review independently matched all four reference PNG byte hashes to their case metadata.
evidence_identity.png_identity_method: Get-FileHash SHA256 over the unmodified PNG file bytes. Images were viewed individually with tools.view_image; no derivative image hash was substituted.
evidence_identity.comparison_scale: All geometry observations compare the candidate at 1x with the reference at one half of its physical dimensions.

observations: The sidecar identifies this exact round-1 run, binary, source, PW5 profile, reader route, menu=true and reader-brightness panel. Both PNG byte hashes match the respective case evidence.
The two lighting rows show brightness 12 and warmth 8, matching the reference values. Both sliders, endpoint icons and value labels are visible and unclipped.

The slider tracks occupy approximately the same logical horizontal extent as the reference. The panel begins about six logical pixels earlier, while its lower divider and the reading progress section remain aligned; no fixed lighting-panel height requirement is established by the supplied assertions.
The status/header hierarchy, heavy heading treatment, grayscale controls and five-tool strip remain visually consistent. The progress thumb, page count and adjacent-chapter actions are visible.

The candidate artwork has approximately 16 logical pixels of horizontal inset on each side, while the reference artwork reaches the screen edges. This is recorded as a framing observation, with its source unresolved by the supplied static evidence.
intentional_differences: The desktop evidence declares frontlight and warmth controls for the selected PW5 profile, without qualifying a physical lighting effect.
Scribe auto brightness is not applicable to this PW5 case.

observations: The sidecar identifies this exact round-1 run, binary, source, PW5 profile, reader route, menu=true and reader-mode panel. Both PNG byte hashes match the respective case evidence.
Four equally sized direction cards are present, with right-to-left selected in black. Single-page, spread and automatic page layout controls are visible, with automatic selected.
The crop-borders toggle is present. The separate split-double-page-spreads row visible in the reference is absent from the candidate.

The reference title row shows the per-book default direction at its right edge; the candidate title row has no corresponding summary despite the sidecar recording right-to-left and remember_book_direction=true.

The direction cards retain approximately the reference's 88 logical-pixel height. Omitting a control row accounts for the shorter panel and higher artwork exposure; that resulting height change is not reported as a separate geometry defect.
The control labels and icons are readable without clipping, and the grayscale selected/unselected hierarchy is clear. The common artwork inset is present here as well.
The sidecar identifies this exact round-1 run, binary, source, PW5 profile, reader route, menu=true and reader-more panel. Both PNG byte hashes match the respective case evidence.
Show tap regions, reverse left/right taps and refresh once remain visible as three distinct actions. The two toggles show off and the refresh action retains its icon.
The remaining action rows preserve approximately 46 logical-pixel spacing and full-width separators. Labels, toggles and the refresh icon are unclipped and retain readable grayscale contrast.

The panel is shorter because the legacy footer-preference section is removed. No supplied assertion establishes a fixed height for this content-dependent panel, so the resulting change in its top edge is accepted.
The progress section, chapter navigation and five-tool strip remain visible below the panel, with More selected. No success claim is displayed. The common artwork inset is present here as well.
intentional_differences: The legacy footer-display choices are omitted in accordance with the artwork-only closed-reader override; they must not restore labels, a bookmark ribbon, notifications or an invisible footer-cycle hit region.

observations: The sidecar identifies this exact round-1 run, binary, source, PW5 profile, reader route, menu=true and reader-orientation panel. Both PNG byte hashes match the respective case evidence.
The reference contains three manual orientation cards: portrait, landscape and reverse landscape. The candidate contains only two, and its modal_item_ids list confirms only portrait and landscape.
Portrait is selected with a black card. The two remaining cards are readable, have approximately the reference's 92 logical-pixel height and fit within the screen without clipping.
The missing third choice expands the remaining cards into two half-width cards instead of the reference's three-column row; this is included in the missing-choice issue.

The panel's top and lower progress divider approximately align with the reference. The status/header and five-tool strip remain visible, with Direction selected. The common artwork inset is present here as well.
intentional_differences: Sensor-follow is absent consistently with has_orientation=false. This capability bound does not remove any manual orientation choice.

suggestions.description: Restore the separate split-double-page-spreads control in the PW reading-mode panel.
suggestions.evidence: The reference has a dedicated switch row below crop borders at approximately logical y=581-635. The candidate ends the mode controls after crop borders, and the expected state explicitly requires crop and split controls. This software control is not covered by the declared hardware capability bounds.
suggestions.recommendation: Expose a reachable split-double-page-spreads switch beneath crop borders, backed by the actual reader preference, and retain the reference row spacing without clipping the progress section.

suggestions.description: Restore the manual reverse-landscape orientation choice.
suggestions.evidence: The reference shows portrait, landscape and reverse-landscape cards in one row. The candidate shows only portrait and landscape; its case metadata records modal_item_ids as only portrait and landscape. The expected state explicitly requires reverse landscape, and sensor absence only bounds sensor-follow.
suggestions.recommendation: Implement and expose reverse landscape as a third manual choice, with a matching enabled card, orientation state and three-column geometry.

suggestions.description: Restore the per-book default-direction summary in the reading-mode title row.
suggestions.evidence: The reference shows the current book's right-to-left default at the right side of the mode heading. The candidate leaves that area blank, although its static state records reading_direction=rtl and remember_book_direction=true.
suggestions.recommendation: Display the actual saved book-default direction alongside the mode heading, using the reference's secondary text hierarchy and right alignment.

limitations: This review covers only the four listed reference pairs and eight individually viewed original PNGs; it makes no full-round clean claim.

Review operations were limited to existing PNG/JSON reads, Get-FileHash and writing this review document. No local application, build, tests, validation suite, smoke test or runtime probe was executed.
The static screenshots establish visible controls and their apparent state, but do not verify click behavior, slider 0..24 bounds, persistence, refresh execution or physical hardware effects.

All four cases show menu=true. Closed-reader artwork-only behavior, absence of invisible footer-cycle hit regions, and interactions after closing these panels are not directly evidenced by this batch.

The candidate artwork is inset approximately 16 logical pixels at each horizontal edge while the reference artwork is full-width. The supplied PNGs and sidecars do not establish whether the same native artwork framing was used; this visible difference is recorded without attributing it to a confirmed reader-viewport defect.
No pen, quality-mode, external-authorization or Scribe-only auto-brightness control appears in these four PW5 cases, so those capability behaviors are outside this batch's direct evidence.
